findings.title: PrettyChat rewrites CHAT_MSG_LOOT/CURRENCY text at runtime; LootHistory compiles its loot/currency patterns once and silently stops recording
findings.locations: modules/Override.lua:292, modules/Override.lua:302, modules/Override.lua:121-127, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:151, LootHistory/core/Util.lua:118, LootHistory/core/Util.lua:147, LootHistory/core/Util.lua:187, LootHistory/core/Util.lua:210
findings.evidence: ApplyStrings sets _G[globalName] on every settings write, latch transition, profile event and, while the combat watcher is armed, every combat boundary (visibility inCombat/outOfCombat). LootHistory caches lootPatterns/currencyPatterns on first parse (`local pats = lootPatterns or Util.BuildLootPatterns()`) and never rebuilds them. After any change, self-loot and self-currency in the other state go unrecorded, with no error. The mechanism is inferred from PrettyChat's own premise and is unverified in-client. No headless suite can see it.
findings.remediation: PrettyChat side (C-01): add a Known Limitations bullet in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md saying PrettyChat rewrites the CHAT_MSG_LOOT/CURRENCY/MONEY/COMBAT_* payload for every addon, that parsers must build patterns from the live global or revalidate them, and that inCombat/outOfCombat modes change these globals at every combat boundary. Name handoff H-1. Add one sentence to docs/scope.md and add SMK-F001 to docs/smoke-tests.md. Cross-repo (H-1, LootHistory): Util.ParseSelfLoot (:145) and ParseSelfCurrency (:208) record the source global values the cache was built from and rebuild when any differs (about 10 string-identity compares per line). Add a LootHistory test that flips a global between two parses. File a LootHistory issue citing F-001. Do not add a PrettyChat public API, bus message or chat filter. Verify in-client with SMK-F001 (/etrace arg1 changes with combat state).
findings.upstream_repo: LootHistory (cross-repo handoff H-1; not a library/standards change)
findings.verify_reason: Mechanism is real: Override.lua:292 writes _G[globalName] on every ApplyStrings pass, and the combat watcher (Override.lua:121-127, PLAYER_REGEN_* at :138) re-runs it at each combat boundary when visibility is inCombat or outOfCombat. LootHistory/core/Util.lua:118/147 and :187/210 cache lootPatterns/currencyPatterns once and never rebuild them. Severity is lowered because the default visibility is 'always' (settings/Schema.lua:120). Under defaults, LootHistory usually builds its patterns lazily after PrettyChat has applied, so it breaks only after a mid-session string edit, toggle, profile change or perf stand-down. Constant breakage needs the opt-in combat modes, and the finding is still unverified in-client. That is silent data loss in a sibling addon, but only on non-default or mid-session paths, so medium rather than high. The remediation and routing (fix the consumer in LootHistory, document it in PrettyChat, add no new API) are sound.

findings.title: Loot tab copies of LOOT_ITEM_CREATED_SELF/_MULTIPLE are dead settings: saved but never applied; Tradeskill copy always wins
findings.locations: defaults/Defaults.lua:39, defaults/Defaults.lua:43, defaults/Defaults.lua:329, defaults/Defaults.lua:333, settings/Schema.lua:15-19, modules/Override.lua:280-305, settings/Panel.lua:243, locales/enUS.lua:58, settings/Schema.lua:446-468
findings.evidence: Headless probe: Schema.Set('Loot.LOOT_ITEM_CREATED_SELF.format','LOOTEDIT %s') returns true, but live _G stays Tradeskill's format. Disabling Tradeskill's copy restores Blizzard's original even though the Loot copy is enabled and customized. The tooltip says the last category wins 'on /reload', but it wins on every pass. /pc test prints both copies. Four tests pin the current behaviour (test_apply, test_panel, test_schema, test_defaults cross-registration cases).
findings.remediation: Keep only the Tradeskill registration. Delete the Loot entries at defaults/Defaults.lua:39-46. Bump SCHEMA_VERSION to 2 with an idempotent profile-scoped step: move categories.Loot.strings[G] to Tradeskill if Tradeskill has none, drop the Loot strings/disabledStrings, prune empty tables, and log one [Migrate] line. Replace the crossRegisteredGlobals block with a load-time assertion that no global is registered twice. Drop the 'Shared with' tooltip branch (Panel.lua:228-247) and its locale key. Update docs (ARCHITECTURE Known Limitations :186, data-flow.md:145, slash-dispatch.md:77, module-map.md:153, smoke-tests T-53). Replace the four tests, and add 'no double registration' and 'migration v2 moves/keeps/idempotent' cases. Regenerate test-cases.md and the README badge in the same commit. Depends on C-02 (F-003).
findings.verify_reason: defaults/Defaults.lua:39-46 (Loot) and :329-336 (Tradeskill) both register LOOT_ITEM_CREATED_SELF/_MULTIPLE. ApplyStrings (Override.lua:280-305) walks Schema.CATEGORY_ORDER, where Tradeskill comes after Loot (settings/Schema.lua:15-19), so Tradeskill always wins. When Tradeskill's copy is disabled, the elseif at :295 restores the original over the Loot write, so the Loot copy's edits never take effect. The tooltip (Panel.lua:243) wrongly says the last category wins 'on /reload', and the comment at Schema.lua:450-451 wrongly says pairs order is non-deterministic. The remediation is sound, and its ordering after R-03 is correct.

findings.title: Migration runner migrates only the active profile (global stamp) and stamps past a step that raised
findings.evidence: `local from = db.global.schemaVersion or 0`, and schemaVersion is stamped unconditionally after runSteps. A failed step is printed and counted as ran. Later OnProfileChanged/Copied/Reset see from == SCHEMA_VERSION and run nothing, so inactive profiles keep the old shape. The PrettyChat.lua:54-56 comment claims the opposite. There is no impact today because the migrations table is empty, but F-002's fix writes the first migration.
findings.remediation: Keep schemaVersion in global. Split the steps into profileSteps (idempotent, shape-detecting, run on every load-pass entry regardless of the stamp) and globalSteps (gated by the stamp). runSteps returns false if any step raised, and the stamp moves only when all steps succeed. Rewrite the core/PrettyChat.lua:54-56 comment. Add tests in tests/test_database.lua: a profile step runs on OnProfileChanged into a second profile after the stamp moved, and a raising global step leaves the stamp unmoved (with -- red under: notes). Watch that RunMigrations (CCN 12) stays under 15, or split it into helpers.
findings.verify_reason: Confirmed in core/Database.lua. :42 has an empty migrations table. runSteps (:85-90) counts a step that raised as ran. RunMigrations (:100-102) reads the global stamp and stamps SCHEMA_VERSION unconditionally. The core/PrettyChat.lua:54-56 comment claims copied profiles get migrated, which contradicts that. The defect is real, but it has no reachable impact today because there are no migration steps, so low fits better than medium. It becomes a live bug the moment R-02 adds the first migration, so it must land before R-02 (keep it as that fix's prerequisite). The remediation is sound.

findings.title: NS.OriginalFormat reports PrettyChat's own override as Blizzard's original when the client lacks the global
findings.evidence: `return (addon and addon.originalStrings and addon.originalStrings[globalName]) or _G[globalName]`. When the snapshot recorded a nil original, the lookup falls through to live _G, which holds the override. The probe returned the PrettyChat-colored Loot string for LOOT_ITEM_SELF with its original set to nil. It shows up in the panel's Original box and in the /pc test Original line. Reachable only after a patch removes or renames a global (PC-R-07 class).
findings.remediation: If addon.snapshotKeys[globalName] is set, return addon.originalStrings[globalName] (possibly nil). Otherwise return _G[globalName]. The panel already shows '(original not available)' on nil. Add a test in test_override/test_render: a snapshot key with a nil original answers nil after ApplyStrings (red under the current `or _G[...]`).
findings.verify_reason: At modules/Override.lua:589-592, `originalStrings[g] or _G[g]` falls through to the live global, which holds PrettyChat's own override whenever the snapshot recorded nil. ApplyStrings already treats snapshotKeys as the authority (:295-302, PC-R-07), so the fix is consistent with that. It is reachable only when a client lacks the global, so low.

findings.title: Degraded install: /pc test and the Test button print nothing after the first run, though the comments and docs claim a chat fallback

The stub at core/DebugLogSetup.lua:71 has `Add = function() end`, and Show only announces once. So the NS.Print default that the comment at Override.lua:663-668 promises can never be reached, and the degraded path prints nothing after the first run. It affects only a degraded install, so low. The remediation leaves the stub's surface unchanged.

findings.title: Panel New box passes gsub's substitution count into Schema.Set as instanceId
findings.evidence: `NS.Schema.Set(formatPath, (value or ""):gsub("||", "|"))` is not parenthesized, so the count reaches Set as rid and is threaded into validate/onChange/announce. There is no effect today because nothing reads rid. This is the same defect class as PC-R-10, which Util.lua:17-20 and Panel.lua:270-272 already guard against.
findings.remediation: Change it to `NS.Schema.Set(formatPath, ((value or ""):gsub("||", "|")))`. Add a spy test in tests/test_panel.lua asserting select('#', ...) == 2.
findings.verify_reason: settings/Panel.lua:281 does not parenthesize the gsub call, and libs/LibKa0s/Schema.lua:432 is `S.Set(path, value, instanceId)`, so the substitution count arrives as instanceId. It has no observable effect today. The same file guards the identical pattern at :270-272 (PC-R-10). The fix is local to Panel.lua; the libs citation is context only, so routing it as non-upstream is correct.

findings.title: Sorted per-category name list rebuilt at four sites; ApplyStrings allocates and sorts 8 tables per pass
findings.evidence: NS.Defaults is static after load, yet four loops each rebuild and sort the names, which gives four places for the PC-16 ordering rule to drift. The cost is unmeasured (no tests/perf.lua, by exemption).
findings.remediation: Keep the remediation, with the rule_ref changed to none (plain maintainability/perf, no standard cited) instead of anti-pattern #55. Publish a memoized NS.SortedStringNames(category) in modules/Override.lua and return the cached array read-only, with a 'do not mutate' comment. collectNames must copy or filter into a new table rather than filter the cached one. Replace the other three loops. Label the perf benefit as unmeasured, and run the SMK-C09 diff to confirm the order is unchanged.
findings.verify_reason: The duplication is real. modules/Override.lua:283-287 is in ApplyStrings and builds and sorts a fresh names table per category on every pass. Override.lua:566-575 (collectNames) is the same loop with a filter. settings/Schema.lua:434-438 and settings/Panel.lua:454-458 repeat the build-and-sort. NS.Defaults is never assigned at runtime (a grep found no writes), so memoizing is safe. The rule_ref is wrong, though. Anti-pattern #55 (anti-patterns.md:64) is about promoting a repeated shape into a SHARED LIBRARY, and it argues that duplication is often the cheaper answer. It does not ask for deduplication inside one addon. The drift risk is also small: all four sites use the default string table.sort. This is a low-value maintainability/perf tidy-up, not a standards deviation.

The tooltip reads 'Reset the strings on the selected category tab to their defaults.' options-ui-§13: its blast radius MUST NOT narrow to the visible tab. findings.remediation: Owner decision. (a) Make it page-wide per the rule: one Schema.ResetRows batch over all eight categories' rows, one [Set] reset Categories line, a new tooltip key (old key removed), an optional confirmation popup, and README/settings-panel.md/schema.md:158/smoke tests updated in the same commit. findings.remediation: Add an at-line comment above core\CoreSetup.lua naming what resolves. Comment only, no reordering. Do it in the same edit as PC-78/79/80/60, and align ARCHITECTURE.md:35 and module-map.md load order with the TOC. Optionally add a test_doc_structure case pinning the hub's load-bearing list against the TOC comments.

findings.title: Authored generator GlobalStrings/split_globalstrings.py is not under tools/
findings.locations: GlobalStrings/split_globalstrings.py, .pkgmeta:39, DEPENDENCIES.md:146-150, docs/common-tasks.md, docs/global-strings.md, GlobalStrings/README.md, tests/prose_waivers.lua:7, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:270

findings.remediation: git mv GlobalStrings/split_globalstrings.py tools/split_globalstrings.py. In the same commit, change main() so that repo_root = dirname(dirname(abspath(__file__))), input_path = repo_root/GlobalStrings/GlobalStrings.lua, output_dir = repo_root/GlobalStrings, and the TOC path is repo_root/PrettyChat.toc. Update the paths in DEPENDENCIES.md, docs/common-tasks.md, docs/global-strings.md, GlobalStrings/README.md, tests/prose_waivers.lua:7, and the regenerate command inside the ARCHITECTURE.md:270 layout-§2 row. findings.verify_reason: The finding is real. layout.md:93 names GlobalStrings/split_globalstrings.py as newly non-compliant and owing the move to tools/split_globalstrings.py, and tools/ does not exist yet. The remediation is inaccurate, though. It says to 'verify the repo-root paths still resolve', but they will NOT resolve after a plain git mv. The script derives every path from its own directory: split_globalstrings.py:117-119 sets script_dir, then input_path = script_dir/GlobalStrings.lua and output_dir = script_dir, and :194 reads the TOC at dirname(script_dir). After the move it would look for tools/GlobalStrings.lua, write chunks into tools/, and still find the TOC by luck. The script needs a code change in the same commit.

findings.title: Combat watcher is a private CreateFrame carrying non-unit events; the standard contradicts itself (events-frames-taint-§1 vs library-stack-§1)
findings.evidence: CreateFrame('Frame','PrettyChatCombatWatcher') registers PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED/_ENABLED. §1 requires AceEvent, and its carve-out excludes a private RegisterEvent for events the client does not filter by unit. library-stack-§1 cites this very frame as the reason AceEvent is 'when used'. Stand-down is correct, so there is no player impact.
findings.remediation: Upstream first (Sprint 0.1): file a WowAddonStandards issue to widen the §1 carve-out to a lazily-created, fully stood-down boundary-event frame, or to state that such an addon records a row. If the rule is kept, add a Documented deviations row keyed events-frames-taint-§1 (trigger: the first additional event, or a second event-registering module). Vendoring AceEvent is not recommended.
findings.verify_reason: modules/Override.lua:120 CreateFrame('Frame','PrettyChatCombatWatcher') and :138-140 register PLAYER_REGEN_DISABLED/_ENABLED. events-frames-taint.md:7 MUSTs AceEvent and forbids per-module frames for ordinary event traffic, and :24 says a private RegisterEvent for an event the client does not filter by unit is outside the carve-out. library-stack.md:24 cites this same frame as the reason PrettyChat needs no AceEvent. The register in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:269-277 has no events-frames-taint-§1 row. This is tension between the two sections rather than a literal contradiction, since library-stack only makes AceEvent 'when used'. The addon still deviates from ef-§1 with no row. Stand-down is correct, so low severity holds and routing the fix upstream is right.

findings.title: Event registrations are a bare loop with no pcall helper and no record of rejected names
findings.evidence: `for _, event in ipairs({...}) do combatWatcher:RegisterEvent(event) end`. A retired event name would raise, or silently deafen the watcher, with no record.
findings.remediation: Add a registerEvent(frame, event) helper: C_EventUtils.IsEventValid front gate, pcall(frame.RegisterEvent), and a rejected-name record in NS.RejectedEvents. Surface it in /pc debug and in the [Init] summary. Add a test using the kit's M.__badEvents to prove one bad name leaves the other registered and is recorded. Keep test_disabled green.

findings.title: Doc set drifted from code in eight places
findings.locations: docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:71, docs/module-map.md:240, docs/settings-panel.md:61, docs/smoke-tests.md:898, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:33, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:147, settings/Slash.lua:243, core/Constants.lua:24-25, settings/Slash.lua:405-408, docs/scope.md:45, .pkgmeta:21, .pkgmeta:25, docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:193
findings.evidence:
The eight drift items:
1. A General-page explainer TextRow and an afterGroup Test button are still described, but both were removed in 8be34c6.
2. The load order omits core/LifecycleSetup.
3. Slash is cited as minor 13; the vendored minor is 14.
4. The STRING_VSPACER comment says 'bespoke 40/60 editor'.
5. A stale IsAddonEnabled 'second reader' comment.
6. scope.md lists a deleted doc index.
7. .pkgmeta cites packaging.md:28 by line number.
8. ARCHITECTURE.md:193 puts all of docs/automated-tests/ out of scope, when the standard only excludes docs/automated-tests/<run>/.
findings.remediation: Fix items 1-5 and 7 only. Rewrite the General-page description in ARCHITECTURE.md:71, module-map.md:240, settings-panel.md:61 and smoke-tests.md:898 as RenderTabbedSchema over Master controls, with the composer's Test leadButton and Reset pair. Add core/LifecycleSetup to the ARCHITECTURE.md:33 load order, in TOC position. Change ARCHITECTURE.md:147 to Slash minor 14. Drop '40/60' from core/Constants.lua:24-25. Reword settings/Slash.lua:405-408 so it no longer counts readers. Change the two .pkgmeta citations to 'packaging-§1' (no line number). Leave scope.md:45 and ARCHITECTURE.md:193 unchanged. Optionally add the test_doc_structure check that the ARCHITECTURE load order matches the TOC file list.
findings.verify_reason: Six of the eight items are real. (1) docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:71, docs/module-map.md:240, docs/settings-panel.md:61 and docs/smoke-tests.md:898 still describe a General-page explainer TextRow and an afterGroup Test button. The current settings/Panel.lua:116-129 has neither: generalAfterGroup only calls Schema.masterAfterGroup, and 8be34c6 removed the paragraph. (2) The load-order line at ARCHITECTURE.md:33 omits core/LifecycleSetup, which PrettyChat.toc:61 loads. (3) ARCHITECTURE.md:147 says 'Slash minor 13', but libs/LibKa0s/Slash.lua:21 is minor 14. settings/Slash.lua:243 is a historical comment ('minor 12, live set restored at 13') and is NOT drift. (4) core/Constants.lua:24-25 still says 'bespoke 40/60 editor'. (5) settings/Slash.lua:405-408 calls the gate 'the second reader of IsAddonEnabled', but there are now readers in Panel.lua:321, Schema.lua:178 and PrettyChat.lua:88. (7) .pkgmeta:21,25 cite 'packaging.md:28', but the rule now sits near packaging.md:39. Cite it by section instead. Two items are REJECTED. (6) docs/scope.md:45's 'doc index' refers to ARCHITECTURE.md's live '## Documentation map' (line 190), which was not deleted. (8) ARCHITECTURE.md:193 names docs/automated-tests/ once as a generated directory 'never enumerated per run', and lines 241-242 do enumerate automated-tests/README.md and RESULTS.md, so the map is compliant.

findings.title: architecture-§4 closed-message-bus MUST binds (a module registers game events), but there is no bus and no register row; the threshold is ambiguous
findings.evidence: The §4 threshold is 'two or more feature modules, or any module that registers game events'. The ## Message Bus section justifies the absence with 'publishes no named message' and a re-check trigger at the first LibStub('AceEvent-3.0'), and neither is the rule's threshold. The clobber hazard cannot arise with one module and one private frame.
findings.remediation: Decide upstream together with PC-84 (Sprint 0.2). If WowAddonStandards narrows the event arm (to modules registering through a shared AceEvent target, or to a second receiver), rewrite the ## Message Bus sentence to cite it. Otherwise add a Documented deviations row keyed architecture-§4 (trigger: a second feature module or a second event-registering module). Do not adopt a bus.
findings.verify_reason: architecture.md:64-65: the MUST binds 'any module that registers game events'. modules/Override.lua:139 registers two events. docs/ARCHITECTURE.md:137-145 (## Message Bus) justifies having no bus by 'publishes no named message' and an AceEvent re-check trigger, not by the rule's threshold. There is no architecture-§4 row in the register (lines 269-277). The rationale in architecture.md:68-71 (the same-target clobber) cannot arise with a single private frame, so the impact is nil and low severity holds. It is right to decide this upstream together with A-08.

findings.title: The vendored automated-test runner cannot record the performance-§12 exemption; RESULTS.md denies an exemption the addon holds
findings.evidence: The runner (kit rev 25) hard-codes a single skip reason ('ships no tests/perf.lua ... rather than a ratified performance-§12 exemption'). automated-tests-§3 requires reason (2), naming performance-§12, when it applies. testing-§1 forbids editing the kit in place.
findings.remediation: Upstream LibKa0s first (Sprint 1.1). testkit/run-automated-tests.sh detects a performance-§12 row under ## Documented deviations in docs/ARCHITECTURE.md (or root CLAUDE.md for a library), or accepts an explicit consumer fact (KA0S_PERF_EXEMPT or an opts file). It emits reason (2) in manifest skipReason and in the standing paragraph. Add a kit self-test with two fixtures and a changelog entry. Tag, re-vendor whole, and re-run at the next release. No hand-edits here.
findings.verify_reason: tests/_kit/run-automated-tests.sh:343-344 sets a single skip note when tests/perf.lua is absent. Lines 838-842 hard-code the 'first reason ... rather than a ratified performance-§12 exemption' paragraph, which docs/automated-tests/RESULTS.md:58-62 reproduces. PrettyChat does hold a performance-§12 row (ARCHITECTURE.md:269). automated-tests.md:126-128 MUSTs recording reason (2), naming performance-§12, when it applies. Upstream LibKa0s testkit/run-automated-tests.sh (v1.55.0) has no exemption detection either, so the fix has to be made upstream and then re-vendored whole. It is a record-accuracy issue with no player impact, so low severity is right.

findings.title: docs/testing.md tells release notes to cite the bare absence of perf.lua instead of the exemption

findings.verify_reason: docs/testing.md:238-239 reads 'The one narrow exception is `perf` skipped because this addon ships no `tests/perf.lua`, which the release notes state out loud.' automated-tests.md:153-154 says an exempt addon's release notes name the performance-§12 exemption rather than the bare absence, and PrettyChat does hold that exemption (ARCHITECTURE.md:373). findings.title: No core/Compat.lua, and the legacy GetAddOnMetadata is called directly; the standard is inconsistent about whether Compat is required
findings.evidence: compat says every addon MUST ship core/Compat.lua. library-stack-§7 says 'AbsorbTracker and PrettyChat carry none', and the documentation-§3 compat-layer.md trigger counts shims in a possibly-absent file. The legacy call is on the degraded-install path only.
findings.remediation: Upstream first (Sprint 0.3): ask WowAddonStandards whether the MUST binds an addon with zero addon-specific shims. If it does, add a minimal core/Compat.lua (TOC before EnvSetup, annotated) with NS.Compat.GetAddOnMetadata owning the legacy rung, have EnvSetup's fallback call it, and update the compat-layer.md N/A row. If it does not, the finding closes by rule change.
findings.verify_reason: core/ has no Compat.lua. core/EnvSetup.lua:75-76 calls the legacy global GetAddOnMetadata directly on the fallback path, which runs only when the library is absent. compat.md:5 says every addon MUST ship core/Compat.lua, and compat.md:25 says every deprecated-API call MUST route through Compat. library-stack.md:88 says 'AbsorbTracker and PrettyChat carry none', and ARCHITECTURE.md:228 records compat-layer.md as N/A. The standard contradicts itself, so the upstream ruling should come first. The impact is small because the call is on the degraded path only.

findings.title: Defaults hard-coded in multiple places (global defaults in Database.lua; Master-controls defaults typed three times)
findings.evidence: savedvariables-§2 says defaults/Profile.lua MUST be the only place a default is hard-coded. enabled=true and visibility='always' each appear in MASTER_SPEC.defaults, in the reader fallbacks and in the clearing arm.
findings.remediation: First write characterization tests for IsAddonEnabled and GetVisibility, plus a test that the global minimap default survives a reset. Declare NS.GlobalDefaults = { schemaVersion = 0, minimap = { hide = false } } and NS.GeneralDefaults = { enabled = true, visibility = 'always' } in defaults/Profile.lua, beside NS.ProfileDefaults. Do not add a new defaults/Global.lua, because savedvariables-§2 names defaults/Profile.lua as the declaration site. defaults/ loads after core/, so assemble Database.defaults.global from NS.GlobalDefaults at OnInitialize. Then read NS.GeneralDefaults from MASTER_SPEC.defaults, IsAddonEnabled, GetVisibility and the General.visibility set arm (Schema.lua:212). The enabled fallback should keep its `== nil` form (savedvariables-§5).
findings.verify_reason: The finding is real. savedvariables.md:33-34 says defaults MUST be declared in defaults/Profile.lua and that it MUST be the only place a default is hardcoded. The code hardcodes them elsewhere: core/Database.lua:34-39 (global schemaVersion and minimap.hide), Override.lua:38 (enabled defaults to true), Override.lua:72-73 ('always' twice), Schema.lua:119-120 (MASTER_SPEC defaults) and Schema.lua:212 (the clearing arm compares against 'always'). The remediation needs one change: the proposed new defaults/Global.lua would itself break §2's 'MUST declare in defaults/Profile.lua'. The global defaults belong in defaults/Profile.lua instead.

findings.title: settings/Schema.lua publishes NS.Schema non-idempotently
findings.evidence: `local Schema = {}; NS.Schema = Schema`. architecture-§3 requires NS.<Module> = NS.<Module> or {}, and every other module uses that form.
findings.remediation: Change to `NS.Schema = NS.Schema or {}; local Schema = NS.Schema`.
findings.verify_reason: settings/Schema.lua:5-6 is `local Schema = {}` / `NS.Schema = Schema`. architecture.md:57 says modules MUST be published via `NS.<Module> = NS.<Module> or {}`. The finding is accurate, and the remediation is a one-line fix.

findings.title: General subcategory draws no Defaults button; the standard is descriptive rather than explicit
findings.evidence: defaultsButton = false. options-ui-§5's header describes a Defaults button on subcategories, and slash-commands-§2 assumes every schema page has one. The omission is recorded only as a redundancy call, with no register row. Graded as a contract gap, not a MUST.
findings.remediation: No upstream ruling is needed, because options-ui-§5 (lines 111/114) already requires the button. On the General sub-page, set defaultsButton = true with a defaultsTooltip. Point defaultsOnClick at the same reset-all implementation, with its confirm popup, that the in-body Reset all settings control and /pc resetall use (options-ui-§12, options-ui.md:260), rather than at a General-only ResetCategory. The minimap-hide allow-list must survive that path (launcher-§3), so keep test_launcher asserting it through the real button. Update docs/settings-panel.md:79. The alternative is to keep the omission and record a documented-deviation register row in ARCHITECTURE.md.
findings.verify_reason: settings/Panel.lua:722 sets defaultsButton = false, and docs/settings-panel.md:79 justifies that only on redundancy grounds. The finding calls the standard descriptive, but it is explicit. options-ui.md:111 gives subcategories a Defaults button, and options-ui.md:114 says the host MUST declare defaultsButton = true with a defaultsTooltip. options-ui.md:260 (§12) says the General page's header Defaults button sits behind the same implementation as Reset all settings and /resetall. That makes this a local deviation that needs no upstream ruling. It also means the proposed defaultsOnClick = ResetCategory('General') is wrong: it would give the General page a Defaults button that does less than Reset all, which §12 forbids.

findings.title: DEPENDENCIES.md omits Pillow for the layout-§4 logo TGA recipe

findings.title: TOC groups lack conventional-position notes (# Core, # Modules, # Settings)
findings.evidence: # Core says nothing about Constants/Namespace/State/Database/PrettyChat. # Modules says only 'the override pipeline'. # Settings still says 'depend on everything else being initialized'. SHOULD.

Put one on the # Core header (:34) covering Constants/Namespace/State/Database/PrettyChat/CoreSetup/DebugLogSetup, whose positions are fixed only by the annotated lines above them. Put one on # Modules (:73). On # Settings (:76), say that Schema/OptionsSetup/Slash are conventional and only Panel (:80-83) is load-bearing. Do this in the same edit as PC-77..80.

PrettyChat.toc:55-61 and :62-67 are the LifecycleSetup and LauncherSetup notes, and both already state 'conventional rather than load-bearing', so they are the compliant parts. The unannotated conventional lines are in the Core group: header :34, lines :44-46 (Constants, Namespace, State) and :51-54 (Database, PrettyChat, CoreSetup, DebugLogSetup). The other two headers are :73 (# Modules, 'the override pipeline') and :76 (# Settings). The :76 header copies the standard's own template text (toc-file.md:105) and does not say which lines are free to move. All load-bearing lines are annotated (:35-39, :41-42, :47-49, :80-83). toc-file-§5 grading says this is one SHOULD row per file, never one per line, so low is right.

findings.title: 11 of 20 source files lack a self-naming first comment
findings.locations: core/Constants.lua:1, core/Database.lua:1, core/Namespace.lua:1, core/PrettyChat.lua:1, core/State.lua:1, core/Util.lua:1, defaults/Defaults.lua:1, defaults/Profile.lua:1, locales/enUS.lua:1, modules/Override.lua:1, settings/Schema.lua:1
findings.evidence: documentation-§9 SHOULD. The *Setup.lua, Panel.lua and Slash.lua files already follow the model.
findings.remediation: Prepend '-- <path> — <one-line purpose>' to each of the eleven, below the vararg line where there is one.
findings.verify_reason: I counted 20 authored files under core/, defaults/, locales/, modules/ and settings/. The 11 listed ones do not name their own path in the first comment. Database, Util, Profile and enUS start with '-- NS.X — ...', which names the namespace, not the path. Constants, Defaults and Schema have no header comment at all. The *Setup.lua files, Panel.lua and Slash.lua do follow the '-- <path> — ' form. documentation-§9 is a SHOULD and puts the header directly under the bootstrap. Caveat: §9 says repos that have not adopted the convention adopt it 'going forward', so retrofitting is good practice here, not an obligation. Where a purpose comment already exists (Database, Util, Profile, enUS, Namespace, PrettyChat, State, Override), rewrite its first line to lead with the path rather than stacking a second header on top.

findings.title: No test pins the Categories tab-strip wrap invariance; options-ui-§13 Testing MUST conflicts with testing-§8 for a library-drawn strip
findings.evidence: No case asserts that the reserved band and every row's y offset are identical across selections when the selected-state art has a different height. The strip is H.TabStrip (library). Deferred with M1-LK-08.

Upstream only: have WowAddonStandards clarify options-ui-§13 Testing to say that for a library-drawn strip (H.TabStrip) the library's suite pins the invariant, and the consumer relies on it under testing-§8. PrettyChat needs no change.
findings.verify_reason: The proposed LibKa0s work already exists in LibKa0s v1.55.0, the version PrettyChat vendors (CLAUDE.md:42). LibKa0s/tests/test_options_tabs.lua:573 has 'a wrapped strip's geometry is IDENTICAL for every value of the selection'. It forces a wrap, checks the chromeHeight band and every row's y offset across selections, and has a '-- red under:' line. It dates from b3e161c (2026-09-16). The vendored tests/_kit/mock_base.lua:102-108 already gives the Options_Tab_Active_* atlases their own height, and LibKa0s tests/test_mock_base.lua:100 checks that the two families differ. testing-§8 says the addon MUST NOT duplicate library-owned cases, so no host case should be added to tests/test_panel.lua. The only thing left is the wording question: options-ui-§13's 'The suite MUST pin the invariant' does not say which suite when the strip is drawn by the library. That is documentation only, so severity is info.

findings.source_id: PC-76 (PRETTYCHAT-B-06, carried, re-measured) + review Step-0 note (RESULTS.md stale by date)

findings.verify_reason: The newest bundle is docs/automated-tests/20260916-184747. RESULTS.md shows it at 1.5.0 with 385/0/385 tests, 46 files, 854 funcs and max CCN 14. That bundle was committed in 80c932f, and HEAD is 29 commits past it (the finding says 30, which is close enough). There are now 48 authored lint files, as claimed. findings.title: architecture-§1 mandates `local addonName, NS = ...` while lint forbids suppressing 211/addonName (eleven files use `local _, NS = ...`)
findings.evidence: The two MUSTs cannot both be met literally for a file that never reads the name. Recorded, not filed.
findings.remediation: Raise upstream as a clarification only. architecture-§1 should read 'destructure both varargs; name the first `_` when the file never reads it', so the collection does not need per-file 211/addonName stanzas that lint.md would allow but that are just noise. Change nothing in the addon.
findings.verify_reason: The tension is real, but the evidence overstates it. architecture.md:7-11 does say 'Every file MUST start with: local addonName, NS = ...'. lint.md:43, however, forbids only a BLANKET ignore. It explicitly allows 'a narrow per-code ignore in the stanza with a comment saying which files and why'. So both MUSTs can be met literally with per-file 211/addonName stanzas. The .luacheckrc:29-38 comment records a local choice to fix the source rather than suppress, not a lint prohibition. The 11 files that use 'local _, NS = ...' are exactly the ones I counted. Filing this upstream as a wording clarification is still reasonable, and no addon change is needed.

findings.title: docs/performance.md claims to be a one-screen answer but runs 230 lines
findings.evidence: Most of the length is the sweep that performance-§12 requires. The page is correct, just not one screen long.
findings.remediation: Cut docs/performance.md down to one screen with the four facts documentation-§3 names. Move the sweep (currently the '## The sweep' section through the Panel next-frame subsection, :26-134) and the PC-R-05 history (:197-224) into a Tier-3 doc, e.g. docs/performance-sweep.md. Register that doc in ARCHITECTURE.md's ## Documentation map and link to it from the page. The register row should keep citing the sweep commit only.
findings.verify_reason: docs/performance.md is 230 lines, and line 4 calls itself 'the one-screen answer'. The page is real under the exemption, but it runs well past that. documentation.md:193 says that when the addon is exempt the page 'shrinks to one screen', listing four facts: it brackets nothing, which of (b)/(c) applies, WHERE the committed sweep lives, and what re-arms the wiring. performance.md:368-369 says the same. The phrase 'where the sweep lives' shows the sweep is meant to be pointed to, not inlined. So the evidence line 'Most of the length is the sweep that performance-§12 requires' is misleading: §12 requires a committed sweep, not one inside this page. That puts it above info, at a low-severity documentation deviation, and the remediation should not be optional. The register row is also the wrong place for the sweep, because §12 says the row carries the sweep commit as the Why, not the sweep text.
